points.why: It frames the meeting as a buy-in problem and says the easiest way to resist an unwelcome conclusion is to attack its inputs.
It says extra detail only adds more to attack, calls contractors a boundary question to settle with leadership, and recommends rebuilding the argument live with them.
It gives a clear swing test and flip point for attrition and contractors, but does not explicitly say to name the value-laden choices openly.
It suggests taking assumptions to the skeptics and notes that solo work stays 'yours', but does not distinguish leaders consulted during the build from those only shown results.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly rejects more detail alone and centres the advice on co-building and sensitivity testing.

notes: It overclaims that a robust swing result 'ends the argument' and that leaders who supply inputs 'can't attack them afterward', which oversells how settled resistance will be.
